name: 17613-prefillheavy-qwen3next80b-tp4
model: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct, bf16. Not substitutable: the setup is about what a prompt costs on a model that is three-quarters linear attention.
hardware: 4x H100 80GB HBM3, NVLink, of one a3 node -- half the node. No router, no external cache tier.
parallelism: TP=4, PP=1, DP=1, no expert parallelism. 512 experts against 4 ranks.
architecture: Qwen3NextForCausalLM: 48 decoder layers on full_attention_interval 4 (12 full-attention, 36 gated-DeltaNet linear-attention), 512-expert top-10 MoE at every layer, 80B parameters with ~3B active; ~160 GB of weights, ~37 GiB per rank at TP4.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=32, warmup the first 10%, bounded at 640 requests with a 1800 s safety cap. ~576 measured requests.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, 4096 prompt tokens in and exactly 128 out, both fixed (no stdev); `temperature: 0.0` and `ignore_eos: true`; no prefix buckets, no prefix reuse and the radix cache off, so every request pays its whole prompt. Seed 17613.
purpose: A document analysis assistant on an 80-billion-parameter model, 32 concurrent users sending 4,000-token prompts for short answers across four GPUs.
launch:
# sglang `serve` CLI form: one `key: value` per line. An indented or nested block is DROPPED
# silently, so everything here stays flat.
model-path: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct
tp-size: 4
enable-piecewise-cuda-graph: true

# TWO SETTINGS IN ONE LINE. It caps how many tokens one prompt-processing forward pass carries (so
# a 4096-token prompt costs exactly two), and at this version it is ALSO the default value of
# `piecewise_cuda_graph_max_tokens` for a non-MLA model -- the ceiling above which the mode above
# is skipped for that batch, silently. NEVER raise this without raising the ceiling with it.
chunked-prefill-size: 2048

attention-backend: fa3
disable-radix-cache: true
mem-fraction-static: 0.85
